title: Require plans to name and wait for external-service state
summary: Add a planner-prompt convention that any plan step calling an external service (GitHub API, CI, deploys) names the state it needs and how the plan checks or waits for it. Add a critic-prompt rule to reject such a plan in round one when this is missing. A prompt test in athena-context covers both. Audience: Athena's planner and critic agents, and the maintainers who judge plans.

defaults_applied.how: A new unit test covers the convention; cargo test, clippy and fmt must pass.
Two short prompt bullets and one test.
The test asserts the actual frame wording, and the verifier runs cargo test.
The test guards the prompt wording. Whether the critic follows it is prose-only guidance.
The prompt wording and the test are plain, with examples.
The goal is that plans stop calling services without their needed state and the critic catches it in round one. The test checks the wording that causes this.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs (PLANNER_FRAME and CRITIC_FRAME, the planner_and_critic_frames_are_short_and_fit_the_budgets test at about line 394, and the reader/producer guidance-text test pattern at about line 437) and crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md and critic.md. The entry point is compose() plus check_budget(); the prompt text is static, so the property is measured by asserting the frame text directly. The change adds no record or data file under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not involved.

The planner and critic prompt files have room: planner 494 tokens left, critic 517 left. Each frame must stay under 500 estimated tokens (existing test). Added text must be short, about 60 tokens each. The contract and the other sets are untouched.
The named record records/failure-classes/2026-10/20261018-100239-xc20.json is read-only owner data and does not change. It is the evidence for the request. Athena handles its status.

The prompt fixture is a unit test in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs, in the style of reader_checks_for_governance_files_and_producer_stops_on_unlisted_ones. It asserts that the planner frame requires naming the needed state and the wait or check, and that the critic frame says to reject in the first round. No LLM is run.
No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/planner.md has a bullet saying that any step calling an external service (GitHub API, CI runs, deploys) must name the state the call requires (e.g. a run has completed) and say how the plan checks or waits for it before the call.

crates/athena-context/prompts/critic.md has a bullet saying to raise a major finding, in the first round, against a plan whose external-service call omits the required state or how it checks or waits for it.

A new test in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs fails if either bullet is removed from its frame. It asserts planner and critic frame text contain the external-service state/wait wording and the critic's first-round rejection wording. Run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
The existing budget test planner_and_critic_frames_are_short_and_fit_the_budgets and all other tests pass, so the prompts stay within token budgets. Run `cargo test`.

No unrelated behavior changes: `git diff` touches only the two prompt files and the athena-context test module. The reader, producer, verifier and contract prompts are unchanged. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` are clean.

out_of_scope: Changing records/ files, including the failure class record and its introspections
Changing the reader, producer, verifier or contract prompts
Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows or token budgets
Running a live planner or critic model to test the convention
Enforcing the rule in code beyond the prompt text and its test
departures: The change is small and prompt-only, so the cost and time are slightly under the reference. The critic-gate change adds some verification risk.
hard_reason: Changes the critic's rejection rule in the run pipeline's plan review, which gates other jobs.
